I honestly think this game has an insane amount of replay ability especially for a historical game. The weird and random outcomes you can achieve playing obscure nations allow for a TON of possible playthroughs as well as the AI acting so differently each time create tons of unique gameplay outcomes. I also really love a lot of the mechanics although warfare can feel so cruel and unfair at times. Either way, its a banger of a game that I always come back to.
An awesome and expansive game with all the rp and althist you can want and a cool coding lang to make games yet still not dumb enough for me to put a title on my mods missions.

I recommend this game but i have to give it a bad rating because of the DLC policy. I know the whole game isn't 350 $ some of the DLC's are cosmetic but essential features like supporting independence and developing provinces are locked behind a paywall. Vanilla is playable but if you want the whole game experience you have to get at least some DLC's. And i mean they aren't cheap either. Some essential DLC's can cost up to 20 $ and the game already costs 40 $. I know these kinds of game are not cheap to develop but i feel they're going a bit to far. The DLC system can be good if you make new content and not make content that should be in the regular game. I would happely pay 60 - 70 $ for the COMPLETE game not 40 + 20 +20 + 15 + 15 +10.

Having spent more than 2500 hours in this game, it is obvious that I've enjoyed it a lot, but I can no longer recommend buying this game.

EU4 is suffering from a server case of featuritis, coupled with the the game running on a single CPU core, the game simply crawls to a halt, even on modern hardware.

Yes, you will indeed learn new things about the game after spending over a thousand hours, but you'll never be able to actually apply what you've learned, as the game simple can't deal with your massive alliance network, and giant armies.
An amazing game that lost its direction. Instead of giving the players more freedom of choice and immersion, devs are taking it away with each update.

Game quality --> Like your heir is 6/5/5 and your ruler is 78 yrs old !

Paradox's expansion and dlc policies --> Your beloved heir dies in a hunting accident, leaving you with a 1/0/2 !

In summary: I don't care about dlc policies. This game is still like 16 years of 5/5/5 Queen Regent's regency to me.

P.S : I simply forgot to write a positive review for my most played game ever (2543 hrs atm). Shame.

Now, I'm no author or writer and I havn't wrote anything much more than a school essay. But when it came to this game I had to write a review, this was my very first paradox game I've played and my father kept suggesting it towards me because I love strategy games. I kind of disregarded his suggestions, but one day I decided to download the demo, and I must say this is by far the best strategy game I've ever played. As I write this i've soaked in almost 900 hours into this game and gathered 80% of the achievements and I have absolutely no regrets. This is one of the best games i've ever played and I couldn't ask for a better strategy gam. However I do have one request to the makers, maybe darken the color of the united Holy Roman Empire or change it altogether lol, but still this game is perfect 10/10 and I would reccomend it to anyone who loves strategy games.

A game that you can sink hundreds of hours into and still learn new things.

PROS:
Tons of gameplay hours for the cost, tons of things to do, virtually a history sandbox

CONS:
Historical accuracy can be a bit... iffy here and there. DLC costs are sky high (hence the recent barrage of negative reviews.

I'd recommend grabbing the base game, Art of War and Common sense. Grab other DLC as you see fit (i.e. If you find that you love playing in Asia, grab Mandate of Heaven, if you love playing merchant republics, get Res Publica, etc.)

Something about this genre just speaks to me. I really really really enjoy playing alternate history scenarios in Paradox games, but I especially love EU because it seems to have more of a historic and narrative feel. Almost as if the history repeats itself and the story is just slightly different based mostly on what you do. Other Paradox games are good, but they feel way more sandboxy to me. EU hits differently.

EU IV is the pinnacle of replayability. Especially with mods, there are some awesome mods for this, you gotta try at least some of them (I loved Anbennar and Post Finem, looking forward to Beyond Typus). Always makes me wanna go and create a mod of my own RPG setting. Maybe some day.

That being said, I am not a fan of the marketing model. Who is? Expensive DLCs that make the whole package worth hundreds of dollars are not cool. Luckily I was able to snatch it on Humble Bundle. Took me a while to finally invest in it and while I don't regret it, I hope EU V will be slightly less greedy in this regard and more of a complete experience on release.

Complete overhauls and undeniable improvements in trade, espionage, and diplomacy meet a beautiful and straightforward interface to modernize and make accessible the grandest of strategy games. Covering every aspect of nation-building between 1444 and 1821 while avoiding the tedium of micromanagement and the confusion of complicated systems ... all the while making every playthrough in every state unique and challenging and enjoyable is something Paradox has refined here. The RPG elements of Crusader Kings 2 still keep that game at the top of my list of PDS titles, but this one has stolen a solid second spot.
This is a wonderful game, but I believe Paradox's DLC policy should be discouraged. Don't buy this from Steam and don't fork out truckloads of money.

The game itself is awesome. Don't need to describe it anymore than that.
The real problem are the very overpriced DLCs. It feels like they release the game half baked and for then charge for the "DLCs" (that act more as deep fixes for the not properly finished game mechanics and content). The price of those DLCs is almost a crime, since they have a price around 50% of the game when was released. And so far there are 5 major DLCs, and many others minors that bring new songs, new soldiers/ships visual, etc.

Personally, it would be very hard for me to consider purchase another Paradox game if they insist in this sale method.

If you plan to play EU4, expect to buy at least a third of the DLC. The base game is missing a lot of huge things but with the DLC the game is fantastic. Risk meets Age of Empires. The learning curve is asinine. I have nearly 1300 hours on the game and I learn something new every play through. The game has fairly decent replay-ability but unless you have a nation you have a particular interest in, you probably wont be spamming a nation. The new expansion Emperor is coming soon so I personally have been playing less because Europe is largely getting an overhaul. Maybe wait until it drops if you're new. No release date yet. Multiplayer is fun too.
Great game, great modding variety, it would be nice if there was an easier way to exit the game, but overall playing is a great experience.

Europa Universalis IV
Recently, I was chcecking my Steam library and shop, looking for some good Paradox games to play. HOI4? Fuck ton of DLCs. CK2/3? Fuck ton of DLCs. Stellaris? Fuck ton of DLCs. And most importandly for this review; EU4---> Fuck ton of DLCs. I really wanted to get into this game since I watched a lot of gameplay from it on Youtube, but the thing that keeps me away is the price. I can't understand how some people just ignore it, and while I do know that EU4 is an amazing game, anti-consumer practices from Paradox are just unacceptable. Not to mention that the content locked behind the paywall is ( mostly ) so basic, that it should have been in the game from the start. I would've liked to write a longer review, but I just can't. The game without the DLCs is a wasteland of content. Even if you have a lot of money, just don't buy this game with DLCs, at least not with original prices. The guilt of spending so much money on a video game will overpower any feelings of fun during gameplay.

Set in the medieval ages of human history, Europa Universalis 4 takes on the world in an unprecendented scale to showcase the possibility of alternate history where you, the player, take control of a country and lead it to triumphant glory or shameful defeat.

Have you ever wondered what it would be like to rule a country? Well, look no further, this game utilizes Diplomacy, Espionage, and Warfare to present its content in a fun and endearing way that makes you keep coming back for more.

Unlike its counter-part, "Crusader Kings 2", Europa Universalis 4 is about controlling a country and not a dynasty. Although there are "heir" and "ruler" features in the game, it's not as in depth as the Crusader Kings series would be.

I reccomend this game to anyone who is an RTS fan. This game is a MUST play.
5/5

As it stands right now, this game is broken unless you buy Common Sense (which the devs seem to be lacking as of late). I love this game, it is quite frankly my favorite game, or more accurate "was" my favorite.

Core features gutted from a previous version that worked wonderfully, was fun to play, and allowed you to challenge yourself now is less useful then a cat. Want to build buildings? Good luck, that lovely city that is your capital can hold 3 buildings! Six if you're super luck (major, major, major if). Want to get more manpower? Good luck with that, you can't spend those lovely Monarch Points on anything but technology, coring, annexing, stomping on rebels, or ideas.

If you thought you had overflowing amounts of Monarch points previously, you've seen nothing yet!

In all seriousness though, they've managed to take a favorite game of mine, and ruin it.

Also, to those who say, "oh, hey, you have the DLC!", I do to test and see what major changes it did bring. Spoilers, nothing. All it added, and I wish I was kidding, was the ability to improve provinces WHICH WAS ALREADY A PART OF THE CORE GAME. No, I'm not joking, and I very, very rarely use capslock, but that's it. They basically broke their game, hid a key feature that was already present in the game previously behind a paywall, and then gave a big middle finger to their audience.

Quite nice painting application. The tools are somewhat odd and counterintuitive at times, and changing colours is tedious. On the other hand, very rarely art packages include a soundtrack and interesting random event chains, so that's a plus.

Not entirely sure, if this fits a production environment, but surely another few hundred hours will remedy that. Strangely addictive though.

It's like that board game risk on bull shark testosterone . If you aren't that good at grand stragety games then you most likley will be confused. However despite this, it's super addictive to stomp everyone in one area and move on to the next.

Very fun strategy game, I've spent over a thousand hours on it and still come back occasionally.
And I'd recommend it if you have friends to play with who already have the DLC as multiplayer lobbies use the DLC of whoever's hosting.
But otherwise, the expansion DLC are easily $200 on top of the price of the base game*. And the latest few DLC have been bug-riddled garbage. The most recent DLC at time of writing made news for being the most negatively rated game on all of Steam and they're still charging $19.99 for it.

Also, if you're not interested in wars and expanding this game probably isn't for you. It's playable without that but gets boring really fast unless you're using mods.
The game is VERY easy to mod, however, and there are a lot of great mods. Check out Anbennar if you get the game.

*They do sales on Humble Bundle periodically that make it worth it but I don't want to base a review on that. It's also pretty easy to pirate the DLC to try them before you buy but don't tell anyone I told you that.
Great game massive depth, looking forward to the new version but suspect this one will still hold strong for year yet.

Pretty decent game. I haven't played a lot so I still haven't learned a lot of its intricacies, but there is no other game where you can reverse conquer Britain as an Indian superpower and have as much fun doing it.

tldr.text: Very Positive (87%): players praise the content and the challenge, but the price draws the most complaints.
Recent reviews are much less positive, and the price remains the top complaint.

details.text: Recent reviews complain a little less about bugs and crashes and about the developers, while complaints about the price have grown slightly.
Players with under 2 hours are much less positive than veterans who have logged over 50 hours.

reason.text: Negative reviews from this period focus on DLC pricing, and reviews blame Paradox for charging too much for expansions and locking base mechanics behind them.
Reviews also tie this to patches that steer the game toward new DLCs, and some say they will be more careful about buying from Paradox.
